svg.title: gov-tla B5 — Elections.tla: the presidential cycle from the appointment of electors to noon on 20 January and the next election day, each rule one guard that TLC shows the model depends on and TLAPS proves
svg.desc: The States appoint electors, the electors vote on one day, Congress counts and announces or sends the choice to the House and the Senate, and at noon on 20 January the old term ends whether or not anyone was chosen (README § Elections.tla). Each of 24 mutations removes one guard, and TLC finds its counterexample at the constants where the guard binds: 579 rows, every one as expected. TLAPS proves the nineteen safety properties under exactly the mutations that break them, and ExecutiveIsFilled under FairSpec by one WF1 step: 1,145 obligations, all proved. Not proved, and TLC's: the witnesses, the counterexamples, that weaker fairness fails and that FairSpec has a behaviour. This models the text's procedure; it is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

text.tspan: : the presidential cycle from the appointment of electors to noon on 20 January and the next election day, each rule one guard that TLC shows the model depends on and TLAPS proves

g.text: The States appoint electors, the electors vote on one day, Congress counts and announces or sends the choice to the House and the Senate, and at noon on 20 January the old term ends whether or not anyone was chosen (README § Elections.tla). Each of 24 mutations removes one guard, and TLC finds its counterexample at the constants where the guard binds: 579 rows, every one as expected. TLAPS proves the nineteen safety properties under exactly the mutations that break

them, and ExecutiveIsFilled under FairSpec by one WF1 step: 1,145 obligations, all proved. Not proved, and TLC's: the witnesses, the counterexamples, that weaker fairness fails and that FairSpec has a behaviour. This models the text's procedure; it is an exercise, not law (README, opening).

text.tspan: Proved · TLAPS · each under its mutations' absence
Proved · TLAPS · one WF1 step, FairSpec
Weaker fairness fails; FairSpec has a behaviour (7 PROPERTY rows)
Proved · TLAPS · all 24, inside the module

svg.text: Checked means TLC explored every reachable state at the constants in the row list. Proved means TLAPS discharged every obligation for every value of the constants the module's named assumptions admit. Sampled means random simulation found no error; this module has no sampled row. "None of these is a claim about law or practice" (README § How the specs are written and checked). The README's summary table gives Elections.tla 579 rows, 24 mutations, 24 witnesses and 1,145 obligations; the results files give 579, 24,
24 and 1,145 (equal).

text.tspan: One election, then the next: the module is

svg.text: Constitution.tla and Executive.tla seat a President and a Vice President in one Elect step. This module is that step, from election day to the
next election day:
the States appoint electors, and the electors vote on one day;
Congress counts, and announces a result or sends the choice to the House and the Senate;
at noon on 20 January the old term ends, whether or not anyone was chosen, and someone holds or acts in the office;
the term runs in two halves, and the next election opens.
It stands alone, like the other modules, and does not replace their Elect.

g.text: the certificates are on their way to Congress
the result is announced; House and Senate may still have a choice to

svg.text: OpenElection clears the college and the lists: "whatever the last election left undecided is moot"

g.text: from election day to noon on 20 January
the first two years of a term
the rest, until the next election day

svg.text: OpenElection: election day again
noon
at the first noon: NoonInaugurates, NoonSucceeds or NoonVacant (TermEnds: once the count is open, finished or not)

text.tspan: The mechanism: who acts at each stage, the guard each rule is, and the mutation that removes it (

svg.text: Each card is one section of the module. A guard is drawn as Guard (M_X → Property): the mutation that removes it, and the safety property its removal must break (module header, MUTATIONS). Brown cards are the States and the electors; teal is the mechanism. Numbered arrows are what moves; the key is below the picture.

text.tspan: The college — Art. II §1, Amend. XII: the States and their electors
Congress — the count and the contingent elections
The States appoint — Art. II §1 cl. 2, cl. 4

svg.text: Appoint(e, c): a State fills seat e "in such Manner as the Legislature thereof may direct" with an elector
pledged to c.
AppointmentOpen: only while stage = "Appointing", election day (M_FAILED_CHOICE →
AppointedOnElectionDay).
MayBeElector(e): no one in Officers (M_OFFICER_ELECTOR → ElectorsHoldNoOffice).
ElectionDayEnds: a seat not filled by now stays empty (New York, 1789).
Abstracted: an elector is a seat some State fills; winner-take-all, districts and the popular vote are whatever
pledges the seats get.

text.tspan: The electors vote — Amend. XII; Chiafalo (2020)

svg.text: Vote(e, p, v): an appointed elector who has not voted names p for President and v for Vice President, "in
distinct ballots".
PollsOpen: only while stage = "Voting", one day (M_LATE_VOTE → SameDay).
TwoNames(p, v): two persons (M_SAME_NAME → CountCanClose).
Habitation(e, p, v): one at least not of the elector's State (M_HABITATION → OneNotAnInhabitant).
Faithful(e, p): an elector in Binding votes the pledge, bound; one outside it may depart, faithless (
M_FAITHLESS → PledgesBind).
ElectorsAdjourn: an elector who has not voted has cast no vote.

text.tspan: Congress counts — Amend. XII, XX §§1–2, 3 U.S.C. §15

svg.text: OpenCount(new): Seated(new), the Congress that assembled on 3 January (M_PRE_XX →
NewCongressCounts).
Sustain(e, g, both): Concur(both), both Houses (M_PRESIDING → CountIsCongress). Ground
"NotAppointed" takes e out of Appointed, the whole number; "NotRegular" does not.
Announce(p, v): PResult, VResult, a majority of Whole (M_PRE_XII, M_PLURALITY → ElectorsChoose;
M_ENTITLED → DevolvesOnlyWithoutMajority) and TwoPersons(p, v) (M_ONE_PERSON →
PresidentNotVP). The certificates are then spent.
No one carries: pList = PTop, the three highest; vList = VTop, the two highest.
CountCanClose: no guard decides it (README § Elections.tla, CountCanClose).

text.tspan: The House chooses the President — Amend. XII

svg.text: HouseChooses(c, Q, Y): by States; Q present, Y for c; before noon or after it.
OnList(c, pList) (M_OFF_LIST → ChoiceFromTheList); HouseQuorum(Q), two-thirds of States (
M_HOUSE_QUORUM); HouseCarries(Q, Y), a majority of all (M_HOUSE_PRESENT) → HouseVote.
A ballot that chooses no one is a stuttering step (thirty-five of them in 1801).

text.tspan: The Senate chooses the Vice President — Amend. XII

svg.text: SenateChooses(c, Q, Y): OnList(c, vList) (M_OFF_LIST); SenateQuorum(Q), two-thirds (
M_SENATE_QUORUM); SenateCarries(Q, Y), a majority of the whole number (M_SENATE_PRESENT) →
SenateVote.

text.tspan: The term, and the people in it — Amend. XXV §1, XIV §3

svg.text: Die(x): a person in Mortal dies. A President's death makes the Vice President President (Amend. XXV §1); in
the first half, that is service Amend. XXII counts (servedLong).
RemoveDisability(x): Congress removes an Amend. XIV §3 disability (relieved).
Midterm: the second half of the term. OpenElection: election day again.
Abstracted: death is the only way an office falls vacant in a term.

text.tspan: Acting as President — Amend. XX §3, 3 U.S.C. §19

svg.text: VPActs: no President, no one acting, a Vice President: acting' = vicePresident.
SuccessorActs: Statute (M_NO_STATUTE → ExecutiveIsFilled, no safety property) and NoVP (
M_SPEAKER_FIRST → ActingOrder): acting' = Successor, the Speaker, one person who never dies.
SomeoneActs == WF_vars(VPActs \/ SuccessorActs): fairness on the two together. Under FairSpec,
ExecutiveIsFilled: proved (ExecutiveIsFilledAlways) and checked.
Qualify, VPQualify: in the term, a President elect or Vice President elect qualifies late, "until a President shall
have qualified"; whoever acted gives way (3 U.S.C. §19(c)).
TwoPersons at every seating (M_ONE_PERSON → PresidentNotVP); Qualified where the office is taken.
ActingOrder: no one acts while there is a President; the Vice President before the statute's officer.
InOffice = the three seats; Qualifications and Disability are over it.

text.tspan: Noon on 20 January — Amend. XX §§1, 3; XXII

svg.text: TermEnds: the clock is Founding or BeforeNoon and the count is open, finished or not. Exactly one of three
steps is then enabled:
NoonInaugurates: Qualified(pElect); the President elect takes office, the Vice President elect too if
VQualified. TermAllowed (M_XXII, M_XXII_SERVICE → TwoTermLimit).
NoonSucceeds: the President elect has died (ElectGone) and the Vice President elect becomes President (
M_XX3_BECOMES → VPElectBecomesOnlyOnDeath).
NoonVacant: no President: none chosen, or failed to qualify, or dead with no Vice President elect.
VQualified: MeetsArticleII (M_UNQUALIFIED → Qualifications), NotDisabled (M_XIV3 →
Disability).

NoonInaugurates, NoonSucceeds, NoonVacant

VPActs, SuccessorActs

text.tspan: The provisions and where the module has them (README §

svg.text: Art. II §1 cl. 2 — the States appoint electors; no member of Congress or officer is one
Appoint, MayBeElector, ElectorsHoldNoOffice
Art. II §1 cl. 4, 3 U.S.C. §1 — election day, and one day for the electors' votes
AppointmentOpen, PollsOpen, AppointedOnElectionDay, SameDay
Amend. XII — two names on distinct ballots, one at least not an inhabitant of the elector's State
Vote, TwoNames, Habitation, OneNotAnInhabitant
Chiafalo v. Washington (2020) — a State may hold its electors to their pledge
Faithful, PledgesBind
Amend. XX §§1–2 — the new Congress counts
OpenCount, NewCongressCounts
3 U.S.C. §15 — a vote is rejected only by both Houses; an elector held not lawfully certified leaves the whole number appointed
Sustain, Appointed, Counted, CountIsCongress
Amend. XII — a majority of the whole number of electors appointed, or the choice passes on
Announce, PCarries, VCarries, ElectorsChoose, DevolvesOnlyWithoutMajority, CountCanClose
Amend. XII — the House: the three highest, by States, a quorum of two-thirds of the States, a majority of all
HouseChooses, PTop, ChoiceFromTheList, HouseVote
Amend. XII — the Senate: the two highest, a quorum of two-thirds, a majority of the whole number
SenateChooses, VTop, SenateVote
Art. II §1 cl. 5, Amend. XII (last sentence), Amend. XIV §3 — who may hold either office
VQualified, Qualified, RemoveDisability, Qualifications, Disability
Amend. XX §§1, 3 — noon on 20 January; a President elect dead, unqualified or not yet chosen
NoonInaugurates, NoonSucceeds, NoonVacant, Qualify, VPQualify, VPActs,
3 U.S.C. §19 — the officer the statute names acts when there is neither
SuccessorActs, ActingOrder
Amend. XXII — elected twice; once, after more than two years of another's term
TermAllowed, WithinXXII, TwoTermLimit
Amend. XXV §1 — the Vice President becomes President
Art. II §1 — President and Vice President are two persons
TwoPersons, PresidentNotVP
the States, on the electors' side: an elector is a seat that some State fills, pledged to a candidate, so winner-take-all, districts and the popular vote
are whatever pledges the seats get;
the House's delegations: a State's vote is given, not built from its members;
the calendar, apart from the order of the stages and a term in two halves;
one-fifth of each House to object, competing slates, and the grounds of objection beyond the two that differ in effect;
who checks a qualification: it is checked where the office is taken;
every way an office falls vacant in a term but death;
the statutory line, which is one person who never dies.
the States, on the electors' side (an elector is a seat some State fills, pledged to a candidate for President; winner-take-all, districts and the popular vote
are whatever pledges the seats get; who shares a State with whom is the constant Inhabitants); the House's delegations (a State's vote is given, not built
from its members, so voting by member instead of by State cannot be expressed); the calendar (stages in order through the opening of the count; a term in
two halves; noon may strike while the count is open or after); the joint session (objections are sustained elector by elector, then one announcement, after
which the certificates are spent and the ballots cleared); one-fifth of each House to object, and the grounds beyond the two that differ in effect (3 U.S.C.
15(e)(2): an elector "not lawfully certified" leaves the whole number appointed, a vote "not regularly given" does not); competing slates; who checks a
qualification (it is checked where the office is taken; Trump v. Anderson (2024) leaves the States out of Amend. XIV s.3 for federal office); the two-thirds
vote that removes a disability; death is the only way an office falls vacant in a term (resignation, removal and Amend. XXV ss.2-4 are in Constitution.tla and
Executive.tla); the statutory line is one person, Successor, who never dies and is never a candidate; Amend. XX s.4 (a candidate's death before the House
or Senate chooses), on which Congress has not legislated, so the lists stand as announced.
Three readings are fixed, and the module header says where:
a tie for the last place on a list admits everyone tied;
the term limit is a qualification checked at noon, so a President elect it bars has "failed to qualify";
Amendment XII's last sentence is read without Amendment XXII.
Three readings are fixed, each stated where it is used: a tie for the last place on a list admits everyone tied (and the rows cannot tell the House's three
highest from four, which needs seven electors); the term limit is a qualification checked at noon, so a President elect it bars has "failed to qualify"; and
Amend. XII's last sentence is read as Art. II s.1 cl.5 and Amend. XIV s.3, not Amend. XXII (NeverThirdTermBySuccession shows what that reading admits).
Service as Acting President is not counted toward Amend. XXII's two years, the halves being too coarse to time it.

svg.text: Safety is the conjunction of the nineteen safety properties in the "Breaks" column (README). Every mutation's three lists agree. The README's and the header's qualifications ("with three candidates", "five States") are the constants of the COUNTEREXAMPLE rows; the HOLDS rows at the other constants are in the matrix below.

text.tspan: , read from Elections-results-2026.11.16.txt: one line per mutation and set of constants, so verdicts at different constants stay apart

svg.text: The unmutated lines are the text at the defaults (every property), then Safety at each set of constants a mutation's rows use (the c- rows), so a COUNTEREXAMPLE in a mutation's block is the mutation's and not the constants' (rows header). Each mutation's lines are its block at the constants where its check binds, then any further constants. 529 INVARIANT rows on Spec, all drawn; no row runs an INVARIANT on another spec. A COUNTEREXAMPLE row's distinct-state count is where TLC stopped, so the column gives the HOLDS rows' count. Not drawn

here: the 16 DEADLOCK rows (all HOLDS), the 24 witnesses and w-nostatute-successoracts, and the PROPERTY rows (below). A COUNTEREXAMPLE not in the README's "Breaks" cell would be marked ≠ README; none is.

text.tspan: Witnesses: what the text allows, reached (24, each violated unmutated)

svg.text: a President; a seat no State filled; an elector who casts no vote; an unbound elector departing from the pledge;
a vote rejected, and a President elect who lacks a majority of the electors the States appointed, made by rejecting electors;
a person voted for as Vice President and left off the Senate's list;
the House and the Senate each choosing;
noon with no President after a finished count; the Vice President elect becoming President; the Vice President acting; the statutory successor
acting;
a President elect and a Vice President elect each qualifying after noon; the count announced after noon; a disability removed;
a President elect dead; succession within a term;
a person elected President twice; more than two years of another's term; a President elect barred by the term limit;
a person twice elected President becoming President again by succession; the next election opening.
REACHABILITY WITNESSES (Never..., each must be VIOLATED under "none"): a President; a seat no State filled; an appointed elector who casts no
vote; an unbound elector departing from the pledge; a vote rejected; a President elect who lacks a majority of the electors the States appointed, made
by rejecting electors; a person voted for as Vice President and left off the Senate's list; the House and the Senate each choosing; noon with no
President after a finished count; the Vice President elect becoming President; the Vice President acting; the statutory successor acting; a President
elect and a Vice President elect each qualifying after noon; the count announced after noon; a disability removed; a President elect dead; succession
within a term; a person elected President twice; service of more than two years of another's term; a President elect barred by the term limit; a person
twice elected President becoming President again by succession; the next election opening.
SuccessorActs never: Amend. XX s.3 without the law it invites ("Congress may by law provide"). It adds no state, so it breaks no safety property and no
witness; it breaks ExecutiveIsFilled.

g.text: M_NO_STATUTE adds no state: it reaches no successor acting (rows file)

svg.text: A state witness is an INVARIANT row, a step witness ([][...]_vars) a PROPERTY row (Elections.tla, Reachability witnesses). A step witness's count is not recorded. Without the witnesses a property could hold only because the state it forbids is unreachable (README § How the specs are written and checked).

svg.text: Liveness. FairSpec adds SomeoneActs: weak fairness on VPActs and SuccessorActs taken together. ExecutiveIsFilled holds
under FairSpec. It fails:
under Spec;
under SpecVPOnly and SpecSuccessorOnly, which each drop one officer;
under SpecEachAlone, weak fairness on each officer separately (see Findings);
under FairSpec with M_NO_STATUTE.
NoBehaviour is violated under FairSpec. No state is terminal.
Vacant == president = NoOne /\ acting = NoOne.
ExecutiveIsFilled == (clock # "Founding" /\ Vacant) ~> ~Vacant.
SomeoneActs == WF_vars(VPActs \/ SuccessorActs); FairSpec == Spec /\ SomeoneActs.
SpecVPOnly, SpecSuccessorOnly: weak fairness on one officer only. SpecEachAlone: on each separately. NoBehaviour == <>FALSE
ASSUME Mut # "M_NO_STATUTE" PROVE FairSpec => ExecutiveIsFilled.
"A leads-to with no quantifier, so one WF1 step: while the office is vacant the Vice President or the statute's officer can act, acting
changes the state, and no step re-enters the founding."
Lemmas ClockLeavesFounding, SomeoneCanAct, ActingFills; no measure.
README § How …, What is not proved: "the one leads-to with no quantifier, and it is proved, by one WF1 step".
"That the weaker fairness conditions (SpecVPOnly, SpecSuccessorOnly, SpecEachAlone) do not suffice, and that FairSpec has a
behaviour at all (NoBehaviour): existential, checked by TLC in the liveness rows."
"Reachability (the Never... witnesses) and the mutations' counterexamples: existential, so TLC's. ElectionsBound is a TLC device
only."
No terminal state: the 16 DEADLOCK rows, all HOLDS (module header, DEADLOCK).

text.tspan: The proofs: every theorem read from Elections-proof-results-2026.11.26.txt, with its hypotheses
Mutations with a COUNTEREXAMPLE on the property (read; the diagram's join by name)
The property's kind (proof module, INDUCTIVE STRENGTHENING; the diagram's summary)

g.text: a flag (FlagFrame); rests on Sizes, VoteSizes, DisjointVotes, MajorityCarries, CarriesIsMajority
a flag (FlagFrame); rests on Sizes, VoteSizes, DisjointVotes, MajorityCarries, CarriesIsMajority
valid, not inductive: TwoNamesOnBallots, Pigeonhole, ClosesUnderInv

svg.text: The README (§ Elections.tla, Proof) says "Eleven properties are flags and prove at the one action that sets each"; the proof header says "Eleven properties are flags set by one action each (FlagFrame)". The module header (PROPERTIES) names the setting actions: ChoiceFromTheList "Flag set by HouseChooses and SenateChooses"; TwoTermLimit "Flag set by NoonInaugurates and Qualify" (two actions each). Every other flag is set by one.
Proof. Elections_proof.tla proves the nineteen safety properties, each under exactly the mutations that break it, and ExecutiveIsFilled under FairSpec and Mut #
"M_NO_STATUTE". Eleven properties are flags and prove at the one action that sets each. PledgesBind needs one strengthening, that a ballot is cast only by an appointed elector.
CountCanClose is proved as valid rather than inductive: in every state whose ballots each name two persons, some pair can be announced, by the pigeonhole over the electors
counted (FiniteSetTheorems). Its hypotheses are M_SAME_NAME, M_PRE_XII and M_PLURALITY, and the proof holds at every number of candidates, where the rows reach three.
DevolvesOnlyWithoutMajority is proved under M_PLURALITY, since a majority of the whole number is also a plurality. ExecutiveIsFilled has no quantifier in its leads-to, so it is
one WF1 step with no measure: while the office is vacant one of the two officers can act, and acting changes the state. That the weaker fairness conditions do not suffice, and that
FairSpec has a behaviour at all, stay with TLC.
"the base module's named ASSUMEs PersonsWF, NoOneWF, SuccessorWF, FiniteWF and CollegeWF (MutKnown and InhabitantsWF are not used). So the theorems hold for every
finite college, every set of candidates, States and Senators, every Inhabitants and every Binding within it".
"the rows' three seats and two candidates, and the bound ElectionsBound, are TLC's business and are not assumed."
"M_NO_STATUTE breaks no safety property, so no safety theorem cites it; it is the one hypothesis of the liveness theorem."
1,145 obligations, all proved; 22 theorems; 71 lemmas on its LEMMAS line.

text.tspan: lemmas: inside the module, and proved (ELECTIONS-PROOF-TERMINATOR-FINDINGS-2026.11.25.md)

svg.text: The module ends at line 1524, its one end-of-module line, and every lemma comes before it (read). Each Mut…Admits lemma says what its mutation admits, as README § How …, Proofs has it.

Until PR #16, a ==== after ExecutiveIsFilledAlways (line 1372) ended the module before them. The 2026.11.17 results file proved 1,121 obligations and listed the 24 on its LEMMAS line, because scripts/proof_results.py reads the whole text (the findings doc § 1, § 3).
With that line removed: 1,145 obligations, all proved, the 1,121 before plus one per lemma (the findings doc § 5; Elections-proof-results-2026.11.26.txt).

text.tspan: What TLC and the prover found in

svg.text: In Elections.tla, checked; CountCanClose is also proved, at every number of candidates:

text.tspan: One person can lead both lists unless the rule is a majority.

svg.text: CountCanClose was added after a probe with M_PLURALITY and three candidates reached a count that could not be announced:
one person had the most votes for President and for Vice President. M_PRE_XII does the same. Under the text's majority rule
TLC finds no such state, with two candidates or three.

text.tspan: The count can also stall on the ballot.

svg.text: Amendment XII does not repeat Article II's "two Persons". If an elector may name one person twice (M_SAME_NAME), a person with
a majority on both lists can be announced for neither office.

text.tspan: The executive power is continuous because of a statute.

svg.text: With M_NO_STATUTE, a term that begins with neither a President elect nor a Vice President elect qualified leaves the office empty
until one of them qualifies, which may be never.

text.tspan: Weak fairness on each officer separately is not enough.

svg.text: Under SpecEachAlone a vacancy lasts forever while a Vice President elect qualifies in one term and none does in the next: the
Vice President and the statute's officer are each obliged only from time to time, and neither ever acts. The fairness that works is
on the two together.

text.tspan: Rejecting electors can make a majority.

svg.text: Two electors are appointed and one votes, so nobody has a majority. Both Houses hold the other not lawfully certified, the whole
number appointed falls to one, and the one vote elects (NeverElectedByRejection).

text.tspan: The quorum rules bind only at some sizes.

svg.text: With three or four States a majority of all the States is already two-thirds of them, so M_HOUSE_QUORUM changes nothing there: its
rows at those sizes hold, with the state count of none. Its other rows use five States, and M_HOUSE_PRESENT's use four. The same
holds for the Senate.
Read without Amendment XXII, Amendment XII's last sentence lets a person twice elected President be elected Vice President
and become President again (NeverThirdTermBySuccession). This is a consequence of the reading the module fixes, not a
claim about which reading is right.

text.tspan: The constants: the row list's defaults, where each mutation's check binds, and
{a, b, c, e1, e2, e3, e4, e5, sp}
{a, b, c, e1, e2, e3, e4, e5, sp}
Where each mutation's check binds (rows file header)

svg.text: M_OFFICER_ELECTOR: e3 holds an office (unmutated, that seat is never filled)
M_HABITATION: e1 shares a State with both candidates (unmutated, e1 can cast no ballot)
M_PRESIDING: e1's vote is open to objection
M_HOUSE_QUORUM: five States, the fewest at which a majority of all the States can lack a quorum
M_HOUSE_PRESENT: four States, the fewest at which a majority of a quorum is not a majority of all
M_SENATE_QUORUM, M_SENATE_PRESENT: the same, with Senators
M_UNQUALIFIED, M_XX3_BECOMES, M_SPEAKER_FIRST: b is not eligible (so b elected is a President elect who fails to qualify)
M_XIV3: b is under the disability
M_XXII: constraint ElectionsBound (elected <= 3), the count of elections being otherwise unbounded
M_XXII_SERVICE: one seat and b mortal: b dies early in a term and a serves out more than two years of it

"The other mutations bind at the defaults. Safety and the deadlock audit also run unmutated at each of these sets of constants (the c- rows), so a COUNTEREXAMPLE in a mutation's block is the mutation's and not the constants'."
Rows. The defaults are the smallest constants that run a whole election: three electors, each held to the pledge, and two candidates. That is 38,180 states. Each mutation runs against
every property at the constants where its check binds, and Safety runs unmutated at each of those sets of constants. Two rows are larger: three candidates (1,301,661 states) and the
constants of Elections.cfg (2,060,728).
The rows cannot reach the House's list of three excluding a fourth person voted for, which needs seven electors.
Elections.cfg: SPECIFICATION Spec, INVARIANTS TypeOK, Safety; "for ad hoc runs and simulation. The checked results come from rows/Elections-rows.txt".
c-cfg-safety checks Safety at the row defaults with 4 overrides: 2,060,728 distinct states, HOLDS.
The constants differ only in Persons, Eligible: the rows add the persons "c, e4 and e5 … for the rows that add a candidate or a seat; unused, they add no state" (rows header).

text.tspan: Rows over a million states, read

svg.text: c-cfg-safety: 2,060,728 distinct states at Mortal={a,b} Inhabitants={{e1,a},{e2,b}} Binding={e1,e2} Contestable={e1,e2,e3}
c-three-safety: 1,301,661 distinct states at Candidates={a,b,c}
p-none-canclose-3: 1,301,661 distinct states at Candidates={a,b,c}
The README says "Two rows are larger"; the rows header says "Two further c- rows are larger". Read, 3 rows exceed a million states, 2 of them c- rows.

text.tspan: From docs/MUTATION-MATRIX-FINDINGS-2026.11.17.md (§ 2, § 7.6, § 8), beside what the records here give

svg.text: "For Elections the grid is 25 mutations, 20 properties (TypeOK plus nineteen), and about a dozen constant sets, giving 490 m- rows out of 579."
Read: 24 mutations other than none (25 values of Mut), 490 m- rows of 579.

text.tspan: § 7.6 What happened when the proof was written

svg.text: "1,121 obligations, all proved by the pinned prover; 25 flip tests, one per mutation, each failing in the lemma that carries the hypothesis."
Read: 1,145 obligations (1,121 until the 24 mutation lemmas came inside the module, ELECTIONS-PROOF-TERMINATOR-FINDINGS-2026.11.25.md § 5); 24 mutations; 26 Mut #
hypotheses across the 22 theorems. No results file records a flip test (flip_test.py writes nothing to the tree).

text.tspan: § 8 What the proof means for the matrix

svg.text: "The proof says, for every finite college and any number of candidates, what 440 rows said at three electors and two candidates."
Read: 465 m- rows are HOLDS (the note's 440 is "TypeOK plus 18 properties per block"; this count also takes the further constants). "The rows are unchanged as of this note"; its
table, of what the rows could become, is below.
